$comment: Divergence registry for the lnwjud-x fork of https://github.com/engasnm111/lnwjud.
Every entry is a behaviour this repository added that the upstream project does not have and
therefore has no reason to preserve. A merge from upstream can delete it while still merging
cleanly, so each entry names the source marker that proves it survived plus the test that
actually exercises it. tests/release/upstream-divergence.test.ts fails if any marker disappears.
Add an entry here whenever lnwjud-x changes upstream-owned behaviour. Do not add upstream-owned

customizations.summary: The fork's sync commands and the release-gate registration of its guard tests live in the root package.json. Resolving that file as version noise during a merge deletes the commands and silently drops upstream-divergence and native-active-project-wiring from test:release-gate, so the guard stops running while CI still reports green.
An absolute path outside every Active Project is attached as a project by the host instead of being refused with 'not registered'.
Path routing and native path-scope enforcement read one shared key list, so no path field can be enforced without also being routable.
A scope refusal names the retry that works, because a vague refusal makes the assistant tell the user to register the folder by hand.
Full Access attaches a new folder without prompting; stricter profiles confirm once per folder. This is the fork's deliberate approval policy.
Attach activates a project at the end of the active list only, never moves the Primary Project, and never re-activates a project the user switched off.
git_status, git_diff and git_log resolve a project from an absolute cwd instead of requiring an active workspaceId.
get_file_info reports metadata for a path without loading content, mirroring the reference tool surface this fork targets.
A goal lease from another project neither authorizes nor blocks a mutation whose workspace was actually read as unfenced; the refusal is retained when fence state cannot be confirmed.
workspace_tree honours the host explicit-absolute-read grant and invocation authorization, so it cannot refuse a path read_file accepts.

The per-request teardown integration test asserts against its own request count instead of upstream's fixed 64 rounds, because 64 full per-request MCP server rebuilds exceed the test timeout on slower hosts. Taking upstream's side of this file reintroduces the timing flake, and a rerun would only hide it.

The dashboard e2e waits for the post-resize reflow before asserting the file list overflows, instead of sampling layout exactly once. Upstream's single sample intermittently read the pre-resize geometry (measured 432/432, which is deliberately non-overflowing) under whole-suite load and failed the release gate on an unrelated merge.
